<a id="consolefeature"></a>

## `ConsoleFeature`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Console.ConsoleFeature` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader`

The in-game console. One key opens an overlay that shows what the framework is doing and lets the user drive its APIs without restarting the game.

This class is the framework half: config, the toggle key, the scrollback, the command registry's error sink, the built-in commands and the choice of surface. What the console does lives in [`ConsoleSession`](#consolesession); drawing is a surface's job ([`IConsoleSurface`](#iconsolesurface)).

A game adapter registers a surface that looks like the game's own windows ([`ConsoleFeature.RegisterSurface`](#consolefeature--registersurface)). It is used whenever it can be built; when it cannot - the room is not loaded yet, or a game update renamed the game's UI assets - the IMGUI overlay (`ImguiConsoleSurface`) is shown instead and the fallback is logged once. The console therefore never becomes unusable.

Game-specific commands do not belong here. The adapter registers its own through [`ConsoleFeature.Register`](#consolefeature--register) and adds tabs through [`ConsolePanels`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.md#consolepanels), which is why the core stays free of any game type.

<a id="consolefeature--escapeguard"></a>

### `static ConsoleEscapeGuard EscapeGuard { get; }`

Who owns this frame's Escape. A surface reports every frame it is on screen ([`ConsoleEscapeGuard.Observe`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.md#consoleescapeguard--observe)) and claims an Escape it closes on ([`ConsoleEscapeGuard.Claim`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.md#consoleescapeguard--claim)); the game adapter asks [`ConsoleEscapeGuard.ShouldBlockWindowedSwitch`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.md#consoleescapeguard--shouldblockwindowedswitch) before the game's own Escape handling switches a fullscreen window to windowed mode. The core names no game type: the adapter owns that patch.

<a id="consolefeature--initialize"></a>

### `static void Initialize(ConfigFile config = null)`

Binds the config, registers the toggle key and the built-in commands, and starts mirroring the CWY log into the scrollback. Called once from [`ModLoaderPlugin`](CwyLs.ModLoader.md#modloaderplugin)'s Awake; calling it again does nothing.

**Parameters**

- `config`: Config file the `Console.*` entries and the `[Keys] console.toggle.*` chords are bound in. Pass the calling plugin's `Config`; when omitted the framework binds them in its own .cfg.

<a id="consolefeature--open"></a>

### `static void Open()`

Opens the console. Does nothing when it is switched off or already open.

<a id="consolefeature--register"></a>

### `static void Register(string name, string description, string usage, string group, Func<IReadOnlyList<string>, string> handler)`

Registers a command and logs that it arrived. This is the call a mod makes; the registry itself ([`ConsoleFeature.Commands`](#consolefeature--commands)) is public too, for anything more elaborate.

**Parameters**

- `name`: What the user types, e.g. `voice`.
- `description`: One short sentence for `help`.
- `usage`: The argument shape, e.g. `voice list|play <name>`.
- `group`: Heading `help` lists it under, e.g. `game`.
- `handler`: The work; receives the arguments after the name.

<a id="consolefeature--registersurface"></a>

### `static void RegisterSurface(IConsoleSurface surface)`

Registers the surface that draws the console in the game's own style. The game adapter calls this once; a second registration replaces the first. The IMGUI overlay stays the fallback whatever is registered.

**Parameters**

- `surface`: The surface.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `surface` is null.

<a id="consolefeature--reportsurfacefailure"></a>

### `static void ReportSurfaceFailure(IConsoleSurface surface, Exception error)`

Called by a surface that failed while running (an exception in its per-frame work). The game-style surface is switched off for the session and, if the console is open, the IMGUI overlay takes over at once. Never throws.

**Parameters**

- `surface`: The surface that failed.
- `error`: What it threw.

<a id="consolefeature--submit"></a>

### `static string Submit(string line)`

Runs a typed line: echoes it, executes it, shows the result and records it in the history. Never throws.

**Parameters**

- `line`: The line as typed.

**Returns:** The command's output, for a caller that wants it (the smoke checks do).

<a id="consolefeature--toggle"></a>

### `static void Toggle()`

The toggle key's action. Opens a closed console and closes an open one - except that a console faded out with the game's hidden UI is revealed rather than closed, so a press always ends with the console visible or gone, never with an invisible open console. Runs at most once per frame: two paths can fire on the same press (the hotkey registry and a surface whose text field has the keyboard), and the second must not undo the first.

<a id="consolefeature--togglechorddown"></a>

### `static bool ToggleChordDown()`

True on the frame either `console.toggle` chord went down. For a surface whose own text field has the keyboard: the hotkey registry is silent then, so the surface asks here and calls [`ConsoleFeature.Toggle`](#consolefeature--toggle) itself.

<a id="consolefeature--write"></a>

### `static void Write(string text, ConsoleLineKind kind = ConsoleLineKind.Output)`

Appends a line to the scrollback. Safe from any thread; multi-line text is split.

**Parameters**

- `text`: The text to show.
- `kind`: How to colour it.

<a id="consolesession"></a>

## `ConsoleSession`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Console.ConsoleSession` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader`

Everything the console does that is not drawing: which tabs exist and which is showing, the text behind each tab, the buttons a tab offers, running a typed line, Tab completion and the history walk. Every [`IConsoleSurface`](#iconsolesurface) drives the same session, so the IMGUI overlay and the game-style window behave identically and a fallback mid-session keeps the selected tab.

Main thread only, like the surfaces that call it.

<a id="iconsolesurface"></a>

## `IConsoleSurface`

interface · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Console.IConsoleSurface` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader`

One way of drawing the console. The framework ships the IMGUI overlay, which needs nothing from the game; a game adapter can register a surface that looks like the game's own windows through [`ConsoleFeature.RegisterSurface`](#consolefeature--registersurface).

A surface only draws. What the console knows and does - tabs, the scrollback, running a line, completion, history - is in [`ConsoleSession`](#consolesession) and [`ConsoleFeature`](#consolefeature), shared by every surface, so switching from one to the other mid-session loses nothing.

The framework calls a surface on the Unity main thread. A surface that cannot be shown returns false from [`IConsoleSurface.TryShow`](#iconsolesurface--tryshow) and the framework falls back to IMGUI; a surface that fails while running reports it through [`ConsoleFeature.ReportSurfaceFailure`](#consolefeature--reportsurfacefailure).

<a id="iconsolesurface--gameuialpha"></a>

### `float GameUiAlpha { get; }`

How visible the game's own UI is right now, 0 (hidden) to 1 (shown). A surface that does not track the game's UI returns 1. Drives `Console.FollowHideUI`.

<a id="iconsolesurface--name"></a>

### `string Name { get; }`

Short name for the log and the smoke report, e.g. `game-style`.

<a id="iconsolesurface--hide"></a>

### `void Hide()`

Hides the surface. Must not throw; hiding a hidden surface does nothing.

<a id="iconsolesurface--tryshow"></a>

### `bool TryShow(out string detail)`

Builds the surface if needed and shows it. Must not throw.

**Parameters**

- `detail`: On success, a short note on what was built (or empty); on failure, why the surface cannot be shown, e.g. which game assets are missing.

**Returns:** True when the console is now on screen.
